name: Hindustan Unilever Ltd
about: Hindustan Unilever is in the FMCG business comprising primarily of Home Care, Beauty & Personal Care and Foods & Refreshment segments. The Company has manufacturing facilities across the country and sells primarily in India. [1]

sections.one_liner: India's largest FMCG company. Revenue growth is up to +14.5%, but the margin has slipped just below its 22.5% guided floor, so growth isn't reaching profit.
business: India's largest FMCG company: 50 brands in 15 categories, sold through 9 Mn+ outlets to 9 of 10 households. FY26 turnover ₹63,763 Cr. [AR FY26]
Revenue mix: Home Care 37%, Beauty & Wellbeing 24%, Foods 22%, Personal Care 15%, Others 3%. Home Care is the largest segment. [AR FY26]
Ice cream was demerged and is reported as discontinued operations. Sales are mainly in India; export split not disclosed. [AR FY26]
Newer channels: e-commerce was 8% of sales in Q2 FY26. Quick commerce was 3% of the business in Q3 FY26, growing ~100% QoQ. [Q2FY26 call][Q3FY26 call]
financial_snapshot: Sep-26 quarter: revenue ₹18,226 Cr (+14.5% YoY), EBITDA ₹4,089 Cr (+8.1%), PAT ₹2,796 Cr (+3.8%). Each line grows slower than the one above. [Numbers]
Last 12 months: revenue ₹68,359 Cr, EBITDA ₹15,654 Cr (22.9%). Reported PAT ₹15,073 Cr includes Dec-25 PAT of ₹6,603 Cr vs ₹2,562 Cr before exceptional items. [Numbers][Q3FY26 call]
Sep-26 operating margin is 22.4%, the lowest in 8 quarters and ~140 bps below 23.8% a year earlier. [Numbers]
Valuation: P/E 39.1x, P/B 8.9x, dividend yield 2.22%, ROCE 28.4%, ROE 31.0%. Price ₹1,861 is 6% above the 52-week low and 25% below the high. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 2.1% over 3 years vs 6.5% over 5. Revenue was flat FY23–25 (₹60,580→₹61,328 Cr); YoY growth since rose 0%→5.7%→7.6%→10.1%→14.5%. [Numbers]
The 14.1% 3-year PAT CAGR is flattered by a ~₹4,040 Cr Dec-25 one-off. Without it, FY26 PAT is ≈₹11,018 Cr, only +3% YoY. [Numbers]
EBITDA CAGR was only 2.1% FY23–26 (₹14,147→₹15,039 Cr). Operating margin has drifted from 25% in FY21 to 23% now. [Numbers]
ROCE fell from 39% to 25% in FY22 and has stayed at 27–28% since, with no upward trend. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings ₹1,672 Cr vs net worth ₹48,830 Cr. Debt-to-equity has been 0.03 for three years, so the company is effectively debt-free. [Numbers]
Net worth fell from ₹51,218 Cr to ₹48,739 Cr over FY24–26 despite ₹25,730 Cr of FY25–26 PAT. Payouts plus the demerger exceeded earnings. [Numbers][AR FY26]
Cash conversion cycle was −89 days in FY26, the most negative in six years, so suppliers fund operations. Debtor days rose from 14 to 19 since FY21. [Numbers]
cash_quality: 3-year CFO/PAT is 1.07. But FY26 CFO of ₹10,999 Cr is only 0.73x reported PAT, or ~1.0x excluding the Dec-25 one-off. [Numbers]
CFO fell 29% from ₹15,469 Cr in FY24 to ₹10,999 Cr in FY26. FCF fell from ₹14,012 Cr to ₹9,667 Cr over the same period. [Numbers]
The 2.22% yield implies a ~₹9,700 Cr payout, about equal to FY26 FCF of ₹9,667 Cr. The ₹2,000 Cr capex plan leaves almost no surplus. [Numbers][AR FY26]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management calls growth volume-led, but Q1 FY27's 10% underlying sales growth was 5% volume and 5% price. Price contributed as much as volume. [Q1FY27 call]
Q1 FY27 'quality of earnings': management cites adjusted PAT +11%, but reported PAT fell 3.2% YoY to ₹2,680 Cr. [Q1FY27 call][Numbers]
The ice-cream demerger was meant to add 50–60 bps of margin from Q3 FY26. Instead, reported margin fell from 23.8% to 23.0%, then 22.4% by Sep-26. [Q2FY26 call][Numbers]
On revenue, story and numbers agree. The promised H2 FY26 pickup happened: YoY growth went from ~0% to 5.7% and 7.6%. [Q2FY26 call][Numbers]
guidance: FY27 will be 'ahead of FY26' and volume-led. No number given; management explicitly declined to commit to double-digit growth. [Q1FY27 call][Q3FY26 call]
EBITDA margin band of 22.5–23.5% over the medium term, reiterated despite commodity volatility. [Q4FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
Pricing: low single-digit FY27 increases guided in February. Then 2–5% was taken in the June quarter, with more 'as cost situation dictates'. [Q3FY26 call][Q4FY26 call]
₹2,000 Cr capex for premium Beauty and Home Care liquids, ~1.5x FY26 capex of ₹1,332 Cr. [Q4FY26 call][AR FY26][Numbers]
Rural demand: no H2 FY27 impact unless rainfall is below 85% of normal. Monsoon/El Niño impact capped at 50–60 bps. [Q4FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: H2 volume growth better than H1, which was 2% [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Revenue YoY 5.7% and 7.6% vs ~0% in H1; Q3 volume growth 4%, highest in 12 quarters

ledger.promised: Low single-digit price growth in H2 if commodities held [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Q3: 5% sales growth vs 4% volume growth, so ~1% price; FY26: 5% vs 4%

ledger.promised: Ice-cream demerger adds 50–60 bps to reported EBITDA margin [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Margin 23.8% Sep-25 → 23.0% Dec-25 → 22.4% Sep-26; no uplift visible

ledger.promised: Margin to stay in guided range despite commodities [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: 22.4% (₹4,089 Cr on ₹18,226 Cr), just below the 22.5% floor

ledger.promised: Low single-digit price increases over FY27 [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Q1 FY27 price ~5% (10% sales growth less 5% volume); Q2 split not disclosed

ledger.promised: FY27 growth ahead of FY26 [Q3FY26, Q4FY26, Q1FY27 calls]
ledger.delivered: H1 revenue +12.3% vs FY26 +5.1%; EBITDA +8.3% vs +2.3%. Full year pending

ledger.promised: ₹2,000 Cr capex in premium formats [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Not yet reported; FY26 capex was ₹1,332 Cr

bull: Revenue growth has picked up for four straight quarters, reaching 14.5% YoY. Home Care grew 14%, its best in 3 years. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
28% ROCE, 0.03 debt-to-equity and a −89-day cash cycle: growth pays for itself, and the ₹2,000 Cr capex needs no borrowing. [Numbers][AR FY26]
Stock is 25% below its ₹2,480 high while EBITDA grows 8% YoY. The 2.22% dividend yield gives some support. [Numbers]
bear: Shrinking margin: in Sep-26, revenue +14.5%, EBITDA +8.1%, PAT +3.8%. Management chose not to pass on all cost inflation. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
A 39.1x P/E on ~3% adjusted FY26 PAT growth and a 2.1% 3-year revenue CAGR leaves little room for error. [Numbers]
Soap volumes falling after 2 years of palm-oil inflation; value brands entering liquids; quick commerce competition intensifying. [Q1FY27 call]
questions: Sep-26 margin is 22.4%, below your 22.5% floor. What brings it back?
Of Q2 FY27's 14.5% revenue growth, how much was price versus volume?
Why has CFO fallen 29% since FY24 while revenue grew?
Ad spend is growing slower than sales. Is margin being protected by under-investing?

annual_report.business: India's largest FMCG company serving 9 of 10 households with 50 brands across 15 categories: home care, beauty & wellbeing, personal care, foods. Turnover ₹63,763 Cr.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.comment: Fabric wash, household care, premium liquids

annual_report.revenue_mix: Pan-India reach across 9 Mn+ outlets. 50 brands spanning 15 FMCG categories: home care, beauty, personal care, foods, beverages, nutrition.
strategy: Radical consumer segmentation across democratisers, power spenders, premiumisers
Create modern premium science-backed brands with digital-first launches
Accelerate footprint in general trade and channels of future
Double-down on fewer bigger bets in high-growth spaces
Enable through AI, cost efficiency, sustainability, talent capability
annual_report.outlook: FY2026 delivered 5% growth, 4% UVG, 23.6% EBITDA margin with sequential acceleration. Management confident in volume-led growth despite near-term macro challenges.
annual_report.capex_plans: ₹2,000 Cr to expand manufacturing in premium Beauty & Wellbeing and Home Care liquids. 45 MW off-site solar park commissioned.

Geopolitical tensions and rapid technological disruption
Consumer spending vulnerability to macro headwinds
Quick commerce and e-commerce channel disruption
